articles.title: Canelo Álvarez v Christian Mbilli: WBC super-middleweight championship – live
articles.summary: Álvarez challenges for Mbilli’s 168lb title in Riyadh. Mexican star fights for first time since Crawford loss. Reach out to Bryan on Bluesky or by email. Here come the fighters. First it’s Mbilli, entering first despite his status as the champion, wearing a black tee and red trunks.
body: No surprises here. Canelo Álvarez has won a 12-round decision over Christian Mbilli to capture the WBC super-middleweight title. The official scores were 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110. (The Guardian had it 117-110).

Mbilli surely needs a knockout to retain his title, yet the urgency is nowhere to be seen. Álvarez is practically inviting the champion to come forward, but the Frenchman remains oddly hesitant to engage. It’s a baffling finish from a fighter whose reputation was built on relentless pressure. Álvarez will be a three-time super-middleweight champion as soon as these scores are tallied...

More of the same. Álvarez in total control. Says Stephen “Breadman” Edwards, the respected Philadelphia-based boxing trainer: “Mbilli is lucky this is not the Canelo of 2018-21. He would’ve been stopped already. Mbilli is not performing well [in my opinion]. He’s outthinking himself.”

articles.title: European football: Kane misses penalty as Dortmund share spoils in Der Klassiker
articles.summary: Bayern Munich held to 2-2 draw after Silva equaliser. Barcelona on top of La Liga after thrashng Alaves. The Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty and hit the post for ⁠ Bayern Munich as Borussia Dortmund snatched a last-gasp equaliser through Fabio Silva for a 2-2 draw ⁠in Der Klassiker…
body: Kane, who collected his prize in a ceremony ⁠in London on Monday, was an unused substitute in the 6-1 German Cup second-round demolition of Magdeburg on Wednesday ⁠but returned to the starting lineup on Saturday, missing from the spot with Bayern 1-0 up. He also hit ​the post, one of four ‌times Bayern struck ‌the woodwork. Silva snatched the equaliser in the 89th minute to leave both ‌teams on 18 points, with Bayern top on goal difference.
In a rollercoaster first half Bayern hit the post through Michael Olise and Ismael Saibari missed a golden chance before the visitors had a goal ruled out by VAR.
Bayern, ‌also hit by injuries to Serge Gnabry and Olise, struck in the 38th minute thanks to Konrad Laimer’s goal on ​the rebound, after his first effort was blocked by Dortmund’s Gregor Kobel.

With the Bayern head coach, Vincent Kompany, recovering after his collapse last week, Bayern’s full-back Laimer was more threatening than Kane, who sent his 56th ⁠minute spot-kick against the crossbar. Dortmund scored through Serhou Guirassy on ​the hour but parity lasted only ​six minutes as Dayot Upamecano tapped in from a Kane ​assist from close ‌range.

articles.title: Zion Suzuki horror own goal haunts Aston Villa to hand Fulham a point
articles.summary: Fulham helped cement Jamie Carragher’s argument that Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. No, they know how to grind out a point on a bad day and can go to Barcelona on Tuesday with some confidence.
body: Zion Suzuki’s own goal denied Unai Emery’s team a fifth win in six games after Nicolas Jackson’s eighth goal of the season had promised to lift a resurgent Villa back into the top third of the Premier League.

But while Villa were made to look below par by a Fulham side making it seven points from the last nine, the home supporters sang long and loud to make their manager know how much he is appreciated round these parts.

The Holte End did not wait long to voice their verdict on the spat between the former England international and the Villa chair. That this came within moments of the whole ground applauding the last post in honour of Remembrance Day was a reminder of the game’s preposterous inclination to take itself too seriously.

Villa fans seemed to be caught between two stools: those who thought Nassef Sawiris had overreacted to a pundit doing his job of seeking clicks, querying whether threatening legal action was going too far; and others who considered it as Villa standing up for themselves.

articles.title: Spurs see off Crystal Palace after Mateta’s early red to pile pressure on Sage
articles.summary: Fortune is not favouring Pierre Sage. Just when the Crystal Palace manager needed a positive result, Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early red card condemned his side to a third straight defeat in the league, leaving their manager’s position hanging by a thread.
body: Goals from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke ensured that Tottenham recorded a third successive victory for the first time in 616 days as they moved into the top half of the table. To put that into context, Spurs have had three full-time managers since then, so it was no wonder that Roberto De Zerbi looked so pleased at full time.

By contrast, Sage’s future is in doubt, given that there was an expectation he could be sacked if they lost this game. While Mateta’s reckless red card did him no favours and Palace managed to stay in the game until Van Hecke’s innovative finish 17 minutes from full time, they now find themselves in the bottom three. Only the chair, Steve Parish, will decide his fate with Liverpool up next at home before the international break. Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank are waiting in the wings.

articles.title: Hamilton claims first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City GP
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton claimed his first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell in qualifying for the Mexico City Grand Prix.
body: Hamilton had been outpaced by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc throughout the weekend but the 41-year-old produced his best lap when it mattered most at the end of Q3 to edge out Russell by nine thousandths of a second.

The seven-time world champion has twice claimed Sprint poles since his move from Mercedes to Ferrari at the start of the 2025 season but will now start a grand prix from the front of the grid for the first time since July 2023 after extending his record tally to 105 poles.
Speaking over team radio after being confirmed as Formula 1's oldest pole-sitter for 44 years, Hamilton said: "Thank you so much, it has been such a long time coming."
Moments later in his first post-session interview, Hamilton added: "That felt great! That feels good! I'm so happy. I'm lost for words. It's been a really challenging weekend."

articles.title: Suzuki makes string of saves before conceding own goal in draw with Fulham
articles.summary: Nicolas Jackson scored his eighth goal in 10 games but an error from goalkeeper Zion Suzuki meant Aston Villa had to settle for a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham.
body: Villa should have gone ahead after 15 minutes when they were awarded a penalty following a review when Sander Berge was penalised for a handball in the box as he jumped with Leon Goretzka at a corner.

With neither Emi Buendia nor Ross Barkley in the line-up, John McGinn stepped up to take the penalty but the Scotland international - who had only ever taken a penalty for Villa in a shoot-out - smashed the ball against the crossbar and over.

The home side nearly paid a heavy price for McGinn's miss straightaway after a Fulham counter-attack, but Oscar Bobb was brilliantly denied the opener by a one-handed save from Suzuki who tipped the ball over.

Villa went in front after Timothy Castagne's error allowed Johan Manzambi to play a ball through to Jackson, who cut inside and beat David Affengruber, before wriggling clear of the recovering Castagne to slide the ball past Bernd Leno.

articles.summary: Tottenham beat 10-man Crystal Palace 2-0 at home to record a third straight win and maintain the pressure on Eagles boss Pierre Sage, with his side dropping into the relegation zone.
body: Jean-Philippe Mateta's 13th-minute red card was followed just 12 minutes later by Archie Gray's headed opener at a corner.

Jan Paul van Hecke's scrappy second-half rebound finish then settled the game to give Spurs three consecutive league wins for the first time since February 2025 and move Roberto De Zerbi's side up to eighth.
But Palace's third league loss in a row, which leaves them third-bottom, came after Mateta was sent off for a late studs-up sliding tackle on Micky van de Ven's Achilles.
Referee Michael Oliver had originally shown a yellow card to the Palace striker, but VAR sent Oliver to the monitor, and he changed his decision to a red for serious foul play.

articles.title: Sovereignty wins Breeders' Cup Classic
articles.summary: Sovereignty won the $7 million Breeders' Cup Classic at Keeneland on Saturday, denying Forever Young a rare repeat in the showpiece of the racing extravaganza. Trained by Bill Mott and ridden by Junior Alvarado, 2025 Kentucky Derby winner Sovereignty seized his first chance at the Classic after he…
body: He was beaten twice to open his 2026 campaign, and his Classic participation was again threatened by a hoof abscess, but Alvarado said he never doubted that Sovereignty could win the Classic.

"What he did today, Sovereignty, it's just spectacular," Alvarado said. "We really wanted to run so bad the Classic last year. I'm just so glad the Godolphin team gave us a chance to keep him in training and get to do what he did today."
Sovereignty settled in well behind pace-setting stablemate Knightsbridge and left no doubt when Alvarado set him loose at the top of the stretch.
Forever Young, who gave Japan a first Classic winner at Del Mar last year, ran just behind Knightsbridge for much of the way but faded to finish fifth.

articles.title: Kane misses penalty as Silva snatches Dortmund draw in Der Klassiker
articles.summary: Harry Kane missed a penalty for Bayern Munich and was punished by Fabio Silva’s late equaliser as Borussia Dortmund earned a 2-2 draw in Der Klassiker.
body: This was Kane's first appearance since his Ballon d'Or win and he was honoured in Munich before kick-off, making his own entrance separate from the other players, but the game itself turned into a Halloween nightmare for him in the second half.

With Bayern leading through Konrad Laimer's goal, Kane saw his penalty strike the crossbar before Serhou Guirassy levelled the match after the Bayern striker had been dispossessed in the build-up. Even his assist for Dayot Upamecano's goal was not enough.

That is because Silva stepped up off the bench to equalise for Niko Kovac's side in the 89th minute and though Lennart Karl hit the crossbar with the last kick of a dramatic game, Dortmund held on to remain level on points at the top of the Bundesliga table.

It was another Englishman, Jobe Bellingham, who had appeared to open the scoring following a mix-up involving Upamecano. But it was ruled out after a VAR check showed Carney Chukwuemeka colliding with the goalkeeper as Bellingham swept home.

articles.title: Bayern Munich star Joshua Kimmich opens up on loss of his father
articles.summary: Saturday’s Klassiker against Borussia Dortmund was an emotionally difficult occasion for Joshua Kimmich, who returned to the Bayern Munich squad following the death of his father. The midfielder had missed recent match es to spend time with his family during an incredibly difficult period.
body: Speaking after the match, Kimmich opened up about what his father meant to him, admitting that returning to football was difficult, but that being back with the team also provided an opportunity to find some normality amid his gr ief.

“My dad was by my side and supported me throughout my entire life. It was difficult to come back, but the world keeps turning. I think about him more than anything when I’m out on the pitch. Nevertheless, it was also important for me to help the team today and find a little bit of normality again. The club, the DFB and everyone around us have given my family and me tremendous support over the past few days,” said (as captured by Sky Germany’s Kerry Hau via @iMiaSanMia ).
There are moments when football understandably takes a backseat, and this is certainly one of them. Kimmich deserves enormous respect for finding the strength to return during such a difficult time.

articles.title: Cincinnati Reds closer Emilio Pagán free agent after declining option
articles.summary: The last-place Cincinnati Reds took another competitive hit as they look ahead to next year, with the decision by closer Emilio Pagán to decline his $10 million player option for 2027.
body: He now becomes a free agent, along with DH Eugenio Suárez and reliever Pierce Johnson, both of whom had their mutual options declined by the club – though neither the Reds nor Pagán are closing the door on a possible reunion.
The deadline for option decisions in all three cases was Oct. 31.

Pagán was among the best closers in the league the last two seasons, including converting 19 of 19 save chances with a 1.88 ERA after returning from a severe hamstring injury in early July. He earned a career-high 32 saves, with a 2.88 ERA, for the Reds' 2025 playoff bullpen.
Barring a new deal by Nov. 2 (5 p.m. ET), he becomes eligible to talk to other teams as the MLB free agency opens.
